title: Temurah 13
description: The first chapter closes with the reach of a beit haperas, whose view the mishna’s rules follow, and the next mishna: birds, meal offerings, communal, partners’ and Temple maintenance property do not effect substitution, Rabbi Shimon’s lesson from the animal tithe, Rabbi’s substitution of name and of body, the burnt offering from surplus funds, and Rabbi Avin’s dilemma left as tiba’ei.
topics: 🌾 How far a beit haperas reaches: three fields and two furrows of a hundred cubits
🧺 No teruma after teruma: partners who separate one after the other, and Rabbi Akiva
🐣 No substitute of a substitute, and Rabbi Yehuda on the offspring
🕊️ Birds, meal offerings, the community, partners and Temple maintenance do not effect substitution
🐑 Rabbi Shimon: why the animal tithe was singled out, and what it excludes
🔢 Rabbi: the tithe’s substitution of its name and substitution of its body
🔥 The burnt offering from surplus funds: Rabbi Shimon, Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Avin’s dilemma
📖 Hadran: chapter 1, HaKol Memirin, ends; chapter 2, Yesh BaKorbanot, comes next

a1.he: שָׁלֹשׁ שָׂדוֹת וּשְׁתֵּי מַעֲנוֹת. וְכַמָּה מְלֹא מַעֲנֶה? מֵאָה אַמָּה, כִּדְתַנְיָא: הַחוֹרֵשׁ אֶת הַקֶּבֶר — עוֹשֶׂה בֵּית הַפְּרָס מְלֹא מַעֲנֶה מֵאָה אַמָּה.

a2.he: וְאֵין תְּרוּמָה אַחַר תְּרוּמָה כּוּ׳. מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי? רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא, דִּתְנַן: הַשּׁוּתָּפִין שֶׁתָּרְמוּ זֶה אַחַר זֶה, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: תְּרוּמַת שְׁנֵיהֶם תְּרוּמָה.

a3.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין תְּרוּמַת שְׁנֵיהֶם תְּרוּמָה, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אִם תָּרַם הָרִאשׁוֹן כַּשִּׁיעוּר — אֵין תְּרוּמַת הַשֵּׁנִי תְּרוּמָה, וְאִם לֹא תָּרַם כַּשִּׁיעוּר — תְּרוּמַת הַשֵּׁנִי תְּרוּמָה.

a4.he: וְאֵין תְּמוּרָה עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה כּוּ׳. מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר קְרָא: ״וּתְמוּרָתוֹ״, וְלֹא תְּמוּרַת תְּמוּרָתוֹ.

a5.he: וְאֵין הַוָּלָד עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה. דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״הוּא״ — הוּא וְלֹא וָלָד.

a6.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הַוָּלָד עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה. דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״יִהְיֶה״ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַוָּלָד. וְרַבָּנַן: לְרַבּוֹת שׁוֹגֵג כְּמֵזִיד.

a7.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָעוֹפוֹת וְהַמְּנָחוֹת אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה, שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר אֶלָּא בְּהֵמָה. הַצִּיבּוּר וְהַשּׁוּתָּפִין אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר״. יָחִיד עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה, וְאֵין הַצִּבּוּר וְהַשּׁוּתָּפִין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה. קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת אֵין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה.

a8.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: וַהֲרֵי מַעֲשֵׂר בַּכְּלָל הָיָה, וְלָמָּה יָצָא?

a9.he: לוֹמַר לָךְ: מָה מַעֲשֵׂר — קׇרְבַּן יָחִיד, יָצְאוּ קׇרְבְּנוֹת צִבּוּר; וּמָה מַעֲשֵׂר — קׇרְבַּן מִזְבֵּחַ, יָצְאוּ קׇרְבָּנוֹת בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת.

a10.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָכוֹל יְהוּ קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״קׇרְבָּן״ — מִי שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ ״קׇרְבָּן״, יָצְאוּ קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת שֶׁלֹּא נִקְרְאוּ ״קׇרְבָּן״.

a11.he: וְלָא? וְהָתַנְיָא: אִי ״קׇרְבָּן״ — שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי אֲפִילּוּ קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ ״קׇרְבָּן״, כָּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַנַּקְרֵב אֶת קׇרְבַּן ה׳ וְגוֹ׳״.

a12.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״וְאֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד לֹא הֱבִיאוֹ״ — כׇּל הַבָּא אֶל פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם שְׁחוּטֵי חוּץ, וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא לְפֶתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם שְׁחוּטֵי חוּץ. אַלְמָא אִיקְּרוּ ״קׇרְבָּן״.

a13.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הָא רַבָּנַן. לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִיקְּרִי ״קׇרְבָּן״, לְרַבָּנַן לָא אִיקְּרִי ״קׇרְבָּן״.

a14.he: וְלָא? וְהָכְתִיב: ״וַנַּקְרֵב אֶת קׇרְבַּן ה׳״! ״קׇרְבַּן ה׳״ אִיקְּרִי, ״קׇרְבָּן לַה׳״ לָא אִיקְּרִי.

a15.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ״, לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר? וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אוֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָעוְגוֹ׳״.

a16.he: לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא יָמִיר אוֹתוֹ״, מַשְׁמַע קׇרְבַּן יָחִיד, קׇרְבַּן צִבּוּר, וְקׇרְבַּן מִזְבֵּחַ וְקׇרְבַּן בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לֹא יְבַקֵּר״.

a17.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: וַהֲרֵי מַעֲשֵׂר בַּכְּלָל הָיָה, וְלָמָּה יָצָא? לוֹמַר לָךְ: מָה מַעֲשֵׂר קׇרְבַּן יָחִיד, וְקׇרְבַּן מִזְבֵּחַ, וְדָבָר שֶׁבָּא בְּחוֹבָה, וְדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת — אַף כֹּל קׇרְבַּן יָחִיד, וְקׇרְבַּן מִזְבֵּחַ, וְדָבָר שֶׁבָּא בְּחוֹבָה,

b2.he: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: לָמָּה יָצָא מַעֲשֵׂר מֵעַתָּה? לִידּוֹן בִּ״תְמוּרַת שְׁמוֹ״ וּבִ״תְמוּרַת גּוּפוֹ״.

b3.he: לוֹמַר לָךְ: תְּמוּרַת שְׁמוֹ — קְרֵיבָה, תְּמוּרַת גּוּפוֹ — אֵינָהּ קְרֵיבָה; תְּמוּרַת שְׁמוֹ — נִגְאֶלֶת, תְּמוּרַת גּוּפוֹ — אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת.

b4.he: תְּמוּרַת גּוּפוֹ — חָלָה עַל דָּבָר הָרָאוּי וְעַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי, וּתְמוּרַת שְׁמוֹ — אֵינָהּ חָלָה אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר הָרָאוּי בִּלְבַד.

b5.he: אָמְרִי: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי רַחֲמָנָא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ תְּמוּרַת שְׁמוֹ, אִיגְּרוֹעֵי אִיגְּרַע? אִין, דְּאָמְרִינַן: מַאי דְּרַבִּי — רַבִּי, וּמַאי דְּלָא רַבִּי — לָא רַבִּי.

b6.he: וְהָא מֵהֵיכָא תֵּיתֵי? אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה דָּבָר הַבָּא לִידּוֹן בְּדָבָר הֶחָדָשׁ, וְאֵין בּוֹ אֶלָּא חִידּוּשׁוֹ בִּלְבָד.

b7.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָמַר דָּבָר הַבָּא בְּחוֹבָה — עוֹלַת חוֹבָה הִיא דְּעָבְדָה תְּמוּרָה, הָא עוֹלַת נְדָבָה — לָא? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עוֹלַת נְדָבָה נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּקַבְּלַהּ עֲלֵיהּ — עַבְדַּהּ תְּמוּרָה.

b8.he: וְלֹא נִצְרְכָה, אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָה הַבָּאָה מִן הַמּוֹתָרוֹת.

b9.he: מַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר לַהּ כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר מוֹתָרוֹת לְנִדְבַת צִבּוּר אָזְלִי — פְּשִׁיטָא דְּלָא עָבְדָה תְּמוּרָה, הָא אֵין תְּמוּרָה בְּצִבּוּר!

b10.he: אֶלָּא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר מוֹתָרוֹת לְנִדְבַת יָחִיד אָזְלִי. מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ הַאי סְבָרָא? רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר! הָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ בְּהֶדְיָא דְּעָבְדָה תְּמוּרָה, דְּתַנְיָא: ״עוֹלָה הַבָּאָה מִן הַמּוֹתָרוֹת עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה״, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר!

b11.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא, וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא, דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: עוֹלָה הַבָּאָה מִן הַמּוֹתָרוֹת עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה, וְאִיהוּ סָבַר: אֵין עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה.

b12.he: אִי הָכִי, דְּבָעֵי רַבִּי אָבִין: הִפְרִישׁ אָשָׁם לְהִתְכַּפֵּר בּוֹ, וְהֵמִיר בּוֹ, וְנִתְכַּפֵּר בְּאָשָׁם אַחֵר, וְנִיתַּק זֶה לְעוֹלָה — מַהוּ שֶׁיַּחְזוֹר וְיָמִיר בּוֹ?

b13.he: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן? אִילֵימָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — הָא אָמְרַתְּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ: עוֹלָה הַבָּאָה מִן הַמּוֹתָרוֹת אֵין עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה!

b14.he: רַבִּי אָבִין הָכִי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ: אִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ תַּנָּא דְּקָאֵי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּאָמַר אֵין מְמִירִין וְחוֹזְרִין וּמְמִירִין, וּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, דְּאָמַר עוֹלָה הַבָּאָה מִן הַמּוֹתָרוֹת עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה, מַהוּ שֶׁיַּחְזוֹר וְיָמִיר בּוֹ?

b16.he: וְאִם תִּימְצָא לוֹמַר: קְדוּשָּׁה אַחַת (אוֹ לָא), אֶלָּא שְׁתֵּי קְדוּשּׁוֹת וְגוּף אֶחָד, מַאי? תִּיבְּעֵי.

messages.text: Continued from 12b: the mishna ruled that one beit haperas does not create another, against Rabbi Eliezer. Asked how far a beit haperas extends according to the Rabbis, Rav Dimi, when he came from Eretz Yisrael, said that Reish Lakish said that Rabbi Shimon bar Abba gave this answer.

A beit haperas extends over three fields, the field that was plowed and the two adjacent fields in the direction it was plowed. For example, if one plowed the field from north to south, each of the fields adjacent to it on the north and south is also considered a beit haperas. But whereas the plowed field is a beit haperas in its entirety, the two adjacent fields are a beit haperas only to the extent of two furrows, one furrow on each side.

notes.he: אותה שדה שהיה בה הקבר ושדה לכאן ושדה לכאן אם דרך בני הבקעה לחרוש שדותיהן מזרח ומערב עושה בית הפרס אותה שדה שבמזרח ואותה שבמערב ואם צפון ודרום חורשין (אותה) בית הפרס אותו של צפון ואותו של דרום ששם גלגלה המחרישה את עפר בית הפרס והעצמות אבל לא לארבע רוחות שאין דרך לחרוש שתי וערב. ואותן שתי שדות גופייהו לא הוו כולהו בית הפרס אלא שיעור שתי מענות מענה לזו ומענה לזו אבל אותה שדה שהקבר בה טמאה כולה דלא ידעינן באיזה מקום ממנה היה הקבר ומשום הכי עושה מלא מענה לכל צד דשמא לאחד לב' ראשיה היה הקבר ומשם הלך לאותה שדה חבירתה מלא מענה דזה הוא שיעור חרישת הקבר דכך שיערו חכמים דמלא מענה ראויות העצמות להתגלגל ע"י המחרישה:
notes.en: Three fields and two furrows: the field in which the grave was, and a field on this side and a field on that side. If the custom of the people of the valley is to plow their fields east and west, it makes the field to the east and the field to the west a beit haperas; and if they plow north and south, [it makes] the one to the north and the one to the south a beit haperas, since there the plow rolled the earth of the beit haperas and the bones. But not to all four directions, since it is not the custom to plow lengthwise and crosswise. And those two fields themselves are not entirely a beit haperas, but only the measure of two furrows, a furrow for this one and a furrow for that one. But the field in which the grave is is entirely impure, since we do not know in which place in it the grave was. And therefore it makes a full furrow on each side, since perhaps the grave was at one of its two ends, and from there it went into the neighboring field a full furrow; for this is the measure of the plowing of a grave, as so the Sages estimated: over a full furrow the bones are liable to be rolled along by the plow.

notes.he: פירש"י אותה שדה שהיה בה קבר ושדה לכאן ושדה לכאן אם דרך הבקעה לחרוש שדותיהם ממזרח למערב עושה בית הפרס אותה שדה שבמזרח ואותה שדה שבמערב ואם צפון ודרום חורשין עושין בית הפרס אותה שדה של צפון ודרום ל' רש"י וזה הטעם ניחא לרבנן אבל מה שפירש"י לרבי אליעזר לא נהירא דפירש כל ארבע שדות שסביב בית הפרס שלו הן בית הפרס והעפר מטמאינן ומאי טעמא הוא זה שאם חרשו ממזרח למערב למה יטמאו צפון ודרום ואם חרשו מצפון לדרום למה יטמאו מזרח ומערב לכן נראה לפרש רבי אליעזר אומר בית הפרס עושה בית הפרס דלעולם מה שנחרש מבית הפרס לשדה אחר שאצלו עשאהו בית הפרס וכן אם נחרש מאותה שדה שניה לשלישית וכן משלישית לרביעית וכן לעולם כולן עושין זה את זה בית הפרס:
notes.en: Three fields of two furrows: Rashi explained: the field in which the grave was, and a field on this side and a field on that side; if the custom of the valley is to plow their fields from east to west, it makes the field to the east and the field to the west a beit haperas, and if they plow north and south, they make the field to the north and to the south a beit haperas. These are Rashi’s words. And this reason works well for the Rabbis. But what Rashi explained for Rabbi Eliezer does not seem right, for he explained that all four fields around his beit haperas are a beit haperas and their earth renders impure. And what is the reason for this? If they plowed from east to west, why should north and south be impure; and if they plowed from north to south, why should east and west be impure? Therefore it seems [correct] to explain: Rabbi Eliezer says that one beit haperas creates another beit haperas, meaning that whatever is plowed from the beit haperas into another field next to it makes it a beit haperas; and likewise if it was plowed from that second field into a third, and from the third into a fourth, and so on forever: they all make one another a beit haperas.

notes.dh: אין בית הפרס עושה בית הפרס
notes.he: דשדה שנחרש בה קבר היינו בית הפרס וכל השדה הוי ספק טומאה ואין אומר כל השדות שסביבותיה [הן] (יהו) טמאות דשמא יצא ממנה עצם כשעורה ונכנס באותן שדות אלא אותה שדה לבדה שנחרש בה טמאה והשאר טהורות ורבנן עד כמה הוא שיעור מקום בית הפרס כי אתא רב דימי אמר ריש לקיש ג' שדות אם היתה טומאה באמצעית כשיעור ב' מענות חוץ משדה האמצעית מלא מענה מיכן ומלא מענה מיכן (בשל) [בשדה] החיצונות הוי בית הפרס ולא רצה לומר ה' שדות כלומר דלכל ד' רוחות של אותו שדה [מאה אמה] (מלא מענה) ליהוי בית הפרס אלא ב' מענות מענה מיכן ומענה מיכן והיינו טעמ' [משום דדרך חרישה נקט] ואין אדם עשוי לחרוש שדהו שתי וערב:
notes.en: One beit haperas does not create another beit haperas: for a field in which a grave was plowed is a beit haperas, and the whole field is of uncertain impurity; and we do not say that all the fields around it are impure lest a bone the size of a barley grain went out of it and entered those fields. Rather, that field alone in which [the grave] was plowed is impure, and the rest are pure. And according to the Rabbis, how far does the area of a beit haperas reach? When Rav Dimi came, he said that Reish Lakish said: Three fields. If the impurity was in the middle one, then the measure of two furrows outside the middle field, a full furrow on this side and a full furrow on that side in the outer fields, is a beit haperas. And he did not want to say five fields, that is to say, that on all four sides of that field [one hundred cubits] would be a beit haperas, but only two furrows, a furrow on this side and a furrow on that side. And this is the reason: [because he took the way of plowing,] and a person does not usually plow his field lengthwise and crosswise.

messages.text: And how much is the full length of a furrow [ma’ana]? It is one hundred cubits, as it is taught in a mishna:
One who plows a field containing a grave, and who may have strewn the bones throughout the field, renders the field a beit haperas up to the full length of a furrow, which is one hundred cubits.

notes.he: היינו בית ארבעת סאה דמאה על (חמשים) [מאה] היינו מקום זריעה ד' סאין דילפינן מחצר המשכן דבמאה על חמשים הוו בית סאתים (ר' יוסי אומר חמשה) וטעמא דר' יוסי לא איתפרש לן:
notes.en: A full furrow is one hundred cubits: that is an area of four se’a, for one hundred by [one hundred] is an area for sowing four se’a, as we derive from the courtyard of the Tabernacle, where one hundred by fifty is an area of two se’a. (Rabbi Yosei says: five.) And Rabbi Yosei’s reason was not explained to us.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: And there is no teruma after teruma. Once one designates produce from his crop as teruma, if he then designates additional produce from that crop as teruma, it is not teruma.

notes.he: דאין תורמין ב' תרומות [גדולה] מכרי אחד:
notes.en: And there is no teruma after teruma: for one does not separate two [great] terumot from one pile.

messages.text: Whose opinion is expressed in the mishna? It is the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, as we learned in a mishna:
In the case of joint owners of produce who separated teruma one after the other,

notes.he: מכרי אחד:
notes.en: Partners who separated teruma one after the other: from one pile.

messages.text: The teruma of both of them is teruma, as each is considered to have separated from his share of the produce.

notes.he: שהרי לשניהם חלק בו:
notes.en: The teruma of both of them is teruma: since both of them have a share in it.

notes.dh: מתני' ר"ע היא דתנן השותפין שתרמו זה אחר זה ר' אליעזר אומר תרומת שניהם תרומה
notes.he: דכיון דשניהם יש להם חלק בו והא דממעטינן מאתם ולא שותפין היינו לענין דכל תרומתן אינו תרומה אבל מקצת תרומתו של זה ומקצתו של זה הוי תרומה:
notes.en: The mishna is Rabbi Akiva, as we learned: Partners who separated teruma one after the other, Rabbi Eliezer says: The teruma of both of them is teruma: since both of them have a share in it. And as for what we exclude from “you,” and not partners, that concerns [a case where] their whole teruma is not teruma; but part of this one’s teruma and part of that one’s is teruma.

notes.dh: ר' אליעזר אומר] תרומת שניהם תרומה
notes.he: [משום] דכל אחד תורם (לחלקו) [לדעתו]. [ר' יוסי אומר] אם תרם הראשון כשיעור שאמרו חכמים עין יפה תורם אחד מארבעים. בינוני' אחד מחמשים עין רעה אחד מששים:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: The teruma of both of them is teruma: [because] each one separates by his own intent. [Rabbi Yosei says:] If the first separated of the measure that the Sages stated: a generous eye separates one-fortieth, an average one one-fiftieth, a stingy eye one-sixtieth. [The bracketed “Rabbi Yosei says” is in the printed text of Rabbeinu Gershom; the daf reads “the Rabbis say.”]

messages.text: The teruma of neither of them is teruma. Since each separated teruma independently, it is clear that neither accepts the separation of the other, and therefore neither is valid.

notes.he: ואפילו של ראשון דכיון דחזר השני ותרם גלי אדעתיה דלא ניחא ליה בתרומת הראשון והוה ליה ראשון תורם שלא מדעת וכן שני:
notes.en: The teruma of neither of them is teruma: even that of the first, since once the second went back and separated teruma, he revealed his mind that he is not content with the teruma of the first, and so the first is one who separates teruma without [his partner’s] consent; and likewise the second.

notes.dh: רבי עקיבא אומר אין תרומת שניהם תרומה
notes.he: פירש"י ואפילו של ראשון דכיון דחזר השני ותרם גלי דעתיה דלא ניחא ליה בתרומה של ראשון והוה ליה תורם שלא מדעת וכן שני לשון רש"י ולא נהירא דאין זה כמו ולא תמורה אחר תמורה דהתם הראשון תמורה והשני אינו תמורה לכך נראה לפרש כמו כן הכא דהראשון תרומה ולא השני וקשה דבפרק ג' [מ"ג] דמסכת תרומות תנן שותפין שתרמו ר"ע אומר תרומת שניהם תרומה וחכ"א אם תרם הראשון כשיעור כו' וא"כ קשיא דר"ע אדרבי עקיבא ונראה לר"י דבשמעתין מיירי כשנתנו רשות זה לזה לתרום ומשום הכי תרומת הראשון תרומה לר"ע שהרי מדעת חבירו תרם והשני אינו כלום דנתן לחבירו רשות לתרום וכבר תרם ורבי אליעזר סבר דתרומת שניהם תרומה דגלי אדעתייהו דכל חד (לא) ניחא ליה בתרומת חבירו אבל התם בשלא נתנו רשות זה לזה לתרום הלכך כל חד אדעתיה דנפשיה תרם חלקו לפיכך תרומת שניהן תרומה מקצת:
notes.en: Rabbi Akiva says: The teruma of neither of them is teruma: Rashi explained: even that of the first, since once the second went back and separated teruma, he revealed his mind that he is not content with the teruma of the first, and he is one who separates teruma without consent; and likewise the second. These are Rashi’s words. But this does not seem right, for this is not like “nor a substitute after a substitute,” since there the first is a substitute and the second is not a substitute. Therefore it seems [correct] to explain likewise here, that the first is teruma and not the second. And it is difficult, for in the third chapter of tractate Terumot [mishna 3] we learned: Partners who separated teruma, Rabbi Akiva says: The teruma of both of them is teruma; and the Sages say: If the first separated of the measure, etc. If so, Rabbi Akiva contradicts Rabbi Akiva. And it seems to the Ri that our passage deals with where they gave each other permission to separate teruma; therefore the teruma of the first is teruma according to Rabbi Akiva, as he separated with his fellow’s consent, and the second’s is nothing, since he gave his fellow permission to separate and he had already separated. And Rabbi Eliezer holds that the teruma of both of them is teruma, since they revealed their minds that each one is content with his fellow’s teruma [the printed text adds “not” here in parentheses, marking it for deletion]. But there [in Terumot] it is where they did not give each other permission to separate; therefore each one separated his own portion with his own intent, and therefore the teruma of both of them is partially teruma.

messages.text: If the first one separated teruma of the correct measure, i.e., one-fiftieth of the produce, the produce is thereby tithed, and therefore the teruma of the second is not teruma; but if the first did not separate teruma of the correct measure, and he separated too little, the teruma of the second is teruma.

notes.he: אחד מחמשים:
notes.en: Of the measure: one-fiftieth.

notes.he: כגון שתרם בעין רעה תרומת השני תרומה ולרבי עקיבא בין כך ובין כך לא הויא תרומה ומתניתין נמי סתמא קאמר הלכך רבי עקיבא היא:
notes.en: And if not: for example, he separated stingily, then the teruma of the second is teruma. And according to Rabbi Akiva, either way it is not teruma; and our mishna too states it without qualification. Therefore it is Rabbi Akiva.

notes.he: שכבר פטרו הראשון:
notes.en: The teruma of the second is not teruma: since the first already exempted it.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: And a substitute animal that was consecrated when it was substituted for a consecrated animal does not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute; rather, it remains non-sacred.

What is the reason, i.e., the source for this halakha in the Torah? The verse states: “And if he substitutes an animal for an animal, then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be sacred” (Leviticus 27:10). The verse teaches that the halakha of substitution applies only to a consecrated animal and its substitute, but not the substitute of its substitute.

verse.he: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ־רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם־הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: One may not exchange or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good; if one does substitute one animal for another, the thing vowed and its substitute shall both be holy.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: And the offspring born of a consecrated animal that was not consecrated itself does not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute.

The reason for this is that the verse states: “Then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be sacred” (Leviticus 27:10), which teaches that only it, a consecrated animal, but not its offspring, renders a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute.
§ The mishna teaches that Rabbi Yehuda says: The offspring renders a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute.
Rabbi Yehuda reasons that when the verse states: “Shall be sacred,” this serves to include the offspring.

And as for the Rabbis, who hold that one cannot substitute for the offspring of a consecrated animal, they maintain that this phrase serves to include one who substitutes unwittingly, so that the substitution is valid as if he had done so intentionally.

notes.he: ולקמן בפרק שני (תמורה דף יז.) מפרש לה כסבור להמיר שחור והמיר לבן זו דגבי קדשים לא קדיש דהוי הקדש טעות וגבי תמורה קדיש:
notes.en: To include an unwitting one as an intentional one: and below, in the second chapter (Temurah 17a), it explains it: he intended to substitute a black animal and substituted a white one. With regard to consecrated items, this is not consecrated, since it is a mistaken consecration; but with regard to substitution, it is consecrated.

messages.text: Mishna

The birds sacrificed as offerings, i.e., doves and pigeons, and the meal offerings do not render non-sacred items exchanged for them substitutes, as only the term “an animal” is stated with regard to substitution, in the verse: “And if he substitutes an animal for an animal” (Leviticus 27:10).

verse.he: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ־רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם־הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: One may not exchange or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good; if one does substitute one animal for another, the thing vowed and its substitute shall both be holy.

notes.he: ימיר בהמה בבהמה:
notes.en: Mishna. Only an animal: “he substitutes an animal for an animal.”

notes.he: כדכתב ואם בהמה אשר יקריבו ממנה קרבן לה' כל אשר יתן ממנו כו'. ולא יחליפנו וגו':
notes.en: Since substitution is stated only with regard to an animal: as it is written: “And if it is an animal of which men bring an offering to the Lord, all that any man gives of it,” etc., “he shall not alter it,” etc.

messages.text: A consecrated animal belonging to the community or to partners does not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute, as it is stated in the same verse: “He shall neither exchange it nor substitute it.” One derives from the singular pronoun in the verse that an individual renders a non-sacred animal a substitute, but the community and partners do not render a non-sacred animal a substitute.
Items consecrated for Temple maintenance do not render non-sacred items exchanged for them substitutes.

notes.he: דגבי תמורה כתיב קרבן וקדשי בדק הבית לא איקרו קרבן כדמפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: Items consecrated for Temple maintenance do not effect substitution: since with regard to substitution “offering” is written, and items consecrated for Temple maintenance are not called an offering, as the Gemara explains.

messages.text: The fact that animals belonging to the community or partners do not render animals exchanged for them substitutes is derived as follows: The animal tithe was included in the category of all offerings, and why was it singled out in the verse: “And all the tithe of the herd or the flock, whatever passes under the rod, the tenth shall be sacred unto the Lord. He shall not inquire whether it is good or bad, neither shall he substitute for it; and if he substitutes it, then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be sacred” (Leviticus 27:32–33)?

verse.he: וְכׇל־מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃ לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין־טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ וְאִם־הָמֵר יְמִירֶנּוּ וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל׃
verse.en: All tithes of the herd or flock—of all that passes under the shepherd’s staff, every tenth one—shall be holy to GOD. One must not look out for good as against bad, or make substitution for it. If one does make substitution for it, then it and its substitute shall both be holy: it cannot be redeemed.

notes.he: דסבירא ליה דקדשי בד"ה איקרי קרבן הלכך לא נפקא לן דלא עבדי תמורה אלא מהכא והלא מעשר בהמה בכלל כל הקדשים היה דעבדי תמורה כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:י׳) ואם המר ימיר וגו' למה יצא דכתיב בדידיה דעביד תמורה אם המר ימיר וגו' מה מעשר קרבן יחיד הוא דעושה תמורה אף כל קרבן יחיד עושה תמורה יצאו קרבנות צבור דמעשר ליתא בשותפות כדאמרינן בפרק בתרא דבכורות (דף נו:) יהיה לך ולא של שותפות:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon said, etc.: since he holds that items consecrated for Temple maintenance are called an offering, therefore we derive that they do not effect substitution only from here: But wasn’t the animal tithe included in the category of all consecrated animals, which effect substitution, as it is written: “And if he substitutes at all,” etc. (Leviticus 27:10)? Why was it singled out, in that it is written with regard to it that it effects substitution: “And if he substitutes at all,” etc. [Leviticus 27:33]? Just as the tithe is an individual offering that effects substitution, so too every individual offering effects substitution, excluding communal offerings; for the tithe does not exist in partnership, as we say in the last chapter of Bekhorot (56b): “Shall be yours,” and not of partnership.

notes.he: מה טעם אין עושין תמורה [שהרי מעשר בכלל כל בהמה היה ולמה יצא להקיש כו':
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon explains what the reason is that they do not effect substitution: [for the tithe was included in the category of every animal, and why was it singled out? To juxtapose, etc.]

messages.text: It was singled out to juxtapose substitution to the animal tithe, to tell you: Just as the animal tithe is brought exclusively as an individual offering, so too, all offerings that render their substitutes sacred are individual offerings, excluding communal offerings and the offerings of partners from the halakha of substitution. And just as the animal tithe is an offering sacrificed on the altar, so too, all offerings that render their substitutes sacred are offerings sacrificed on the altar, excluding items consecrated for Temple maintenance from the halakha of substitution.
Gemara
The Sages taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: consecrated for Temple maintenance do not render non-sacred items exchanged for them substitutes

messages.text: One might have thought that items consecrated for Temple maintenance render non-sacred items exchanged for them substitutes. Therefore, the verse states: “And if it is an animal of which men bring an offering to the Lord…he shall not alter it, nor substitute it, good for bad” (Leviticus 27:9–10). This teaches that the halakha of substitution applies to that which is called an offering, excluding items consecrated for Temple maintenance, which are not called an offering.

verse.he: וְאִם־בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ לַיהֹוָה יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃ לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ־רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם־הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: If [the vow concerns] any animal that may be brought as an offering to GOD, any such that may be given to GOD shall be holy. One may not exchange or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good; if one does substitute one animal for another, the thing vowed and its substitute shall both be holy.

notes.he: ואם (כל) בהמה אשר יקריבו ממנה וגו' וכתיב בתריה לא יחליפנו:
notes.en: Gemara. Offering: “And if it is an animal of which men bring an offering,” etc., and after it is written: “He shall not alter it.”

messages.text: And are items consecrated for Temple maintenance not called offerings? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: which are not called an offering

messages.text: The verse states with regard to sacrificial animals: “Or who slaughters it outside the camp, and has not brought it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to the Lord before the Tabernacle of the Lord” (Leviticus 17:3–4). If the verse had mentioned just the word “offering,” I would derive that the prohibition against slaughtering outside the Temple applies even to items consecrated for Temple maintenance, as they too are called offerings,

verse.he: אִישׁ אִישׁ מִבֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁחַט שׁוֹר אוֹ־כֶשֶׂב אוֹ־עֵז בַּמַּחֲנֶה אוֹ אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁחַט מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה׃ וְאֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד לֹא הֱבִיאוֹ לְהַקְרִיב קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה לִפְנֵי מִשְׁכַּן יְהֹוָה דָּם יֵחָשֵׁב לָאִישׁ הַהוּא דָּם שָׁפָךְ וְנִכְרַת הָאִישׁ הַהוּא מִקֶּרֶב עַמּוֹ׃
verse.en: Regarding anyone of the house of Israel who slaughters an ox or sheep or goat in the camp, or does so outside the camp, and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to GOD, before GOD’s Tabernacle: bloodguilt shall be imputed to them; having shed blood, that person shall be cut off from among their people.

notes.he: גבי שחוטי חוץ קאי והאי אי לישנא דתורת כהנים הוא כדאמרינן בכמה דוכתי או אינו כו'. גבי שחוטי חוץ דדריש לעיל מהא מילתא להאי קרבן לדרשא אחרינא דקתני קרבן על הקרבן הוא חייב כרת בחוץ ואינו חייב כרת על חולין בפנים ועלה תני אי קרבן כלומר אי דרשינן להאי קרבן להכי משמע אפילו קדשי בד"ה כו'. ואית דאמרי או משום דכתיב התם או אשר ישחט ולאו מילתא היא:
notes.en: If “offering,” I would understand, etc.: this refers to [the passage of] slaughtering outside [the Temple]. And this “if” is the language of Torat Kohanim, as we say in many places: “Or is it not,” etc. Concerning slaughtering outside, [the baraita] earlier expounded this same word “offering” for another exposition, as it teaches: “Offering”: for an offering one is liable to karet outside, and one is not liable to karet for non-sacred animals [slaughtered] inside. And on this it teaches: If “offering”; that is to say, if we expound this “offering” in this way, it would imply even items consecrated for Temple maintenance, etc. And some say [it is “or”] because it is written there: “or who slaughters”; but that is not so.

notes.he: סתמן בעלי מומין ואינן ראויין לאהל מועד מ"מ קרבן איקרו:
notes.en: Items consecrated for Temple maintenance: ordinarily they are blemished and are not fit for the Tent of Meeting; nevertheless they are called an offering.

notes.he: והתניא] אי קרבן דכתיב או אשר ישחט מחוץ למחנה ואל פתח אהל מועד לא הביאו להקריב קרבן לה' [שומע אני] (שומעני) אף קדשי בדק הבית יהא חייב משום שחוטי חוץ ואלו לא נקדשו להקריב עצמן אלא לדמיהן:
notes.en: [And isn’t it taught:] If “offering,” as it is written: “Or who slaughters it outside the camp, and has not brought it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to the Lord,” I would understand that even for items consecrated for Temple maintenance one would be liable for slaughtering outside, though these were not consecrated to be sacrificed themselves but for their value.

messages.text: as is stated in the matter of the spoils of the war against Midian: “And we have brought the Lord’s offering, what every man has gotten, of jewels of gold, armlets, and bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and girdles, to make atonement for our souls before the Lord” (Numbers 31:50). These were certainly not items consecrated for the altar.

verse.he: וַנַּקְרֵב אֶת־קׇרְבַּן יְהֹוָה אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר מָצָא כְלִי־זָהָב אֶצְעָדָה וְצָמִיד טַבַּעַת עָגִיל וְכוּמָז לְכַפֵּר עַל־נַפְשֹׁתֵינוּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: So we have brought as an offering to GOD such articles of gold as each of us came upon: armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and pendants, uncertain; cf. Exod. 35.22. that expiation may be made for our persons before GOD.”

messages.text: Therefore the verse states: “And to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he did not bring it” (Leviticus 17:4), to teach that for any item that is fit to come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, i.e., that is fit to be sacrificed, one is liable for it due to the prohibition against slaughtering offerings outside of the Temple courtyard. And by contrast, for any animal that is not fit to come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, one is not liable for it due to the prohibition against slaughtering offerings outside of the Temple courtyard.

verse.he: וְאֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד לֹא הֱבִיאוֹ לְהַקְרִיב קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה לִפְנֵי מִשְׁכַּן יְהֹוָה דָּם יֵחָשֵׁב לָאִישׁ הַהוּא דָּם שָׁפָךְ וְנִכְרַת הָאִישׁ הַהוּא מִקֶּרֶב עַמּוֹ׃
verse.en: and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to GOD, before GOD’s Tabernacle: bloodguilt shall be imputed to them; having shed blood, that person shall be cut off from among their people.

messages.text: Evidently, as a verse is necessary to exclude items consecrated for Temple maintenance, such items are generally called an offering, contrary to the first baraita cited.
This is not difficult. This second baraita is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, whereas that first baraita is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis.

notes.he: הא רבי דמוקי לקמן למה יצא מעשר לדרשא אחרינא ולא למעוטי קרבנות בדק הבית אלמא סבירא ליה דקדשי בדק הבית לא איקרו קרבן ולא איצטריך קרא למעוטינהו. והא ר' שמעון דסבירא ליה דלהכי יצא מעשר למעוטינהו אלמא משום דסבירא ליה דאיקרו קרבן:
notes.en: This is not difficult: this is Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who below interprets “why was the tithe singled out” for a different exposition, and not to exclude offerings of Temple maintenance. Evidently he holds that items consecrated for Temple maintenance are not called an offering, and no verse was needed to exclude them. And this is Rabbi Shimon, who holds that the tithe was singled out for this, to exclude them; evidently, because he holds that they are called an offering. [Rabbeinu Gershom reads “Rabbi” here where the daf reads “the Rabbis.”]

messages.text: According to the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, items consecrated for Temple maintenance are in fact called an offering, and therefore in the mishna he derives that items consecrated for Temple maintenance are excluded from the halakhot of substitution from the juxtaposition with the animal tithe, not from word “offering.” According to the opinion of the Rabbis, items consecrated for Temple maintenance are not called an offering, and they therefore derive the halakha from the word “offering.”

notes.he: דמתניתין איקרו קרבן ומש"ה ממעט להו איהו מהיקשא דמעשר בהמה ולא מקרבן:
notes.en: According to Rabbi Shimon: of our mishna, they are called an offering, and therefore he excludes them by the juxtaposition with the animal tithe, and not from “offering.”

messages.text: Rashi and Rabbeinu Gershom also record a version of Rabbi Ḥanina’s answer that reads “Rabbi” (Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi) in place of “the Rabbis.”
And according to the opinion of the Rabbis, are items consecrated for Temple maintenance not called an offering? But isn’t it written: “And we have brought the Lord’s offering” (Numbers 31:50)?
messages.quote: According to the opinion of the Rabbis, items consecrated for Temple maintenance are not called an offering

verse.he: וַנַּקְרֵב אֶת־קׇרְבַּן יְהֹוָה אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר מָצָא כְלִי־זָהָב אֶצְעָדָה וְצָמִיד טַבַּעַת עָגִיל וְכוּמָז לְכַפֵּר עַל־נַפְשֹׁתֵינוּ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: So we have brought as an offering to GOD such articles of gold as each of us came upon: armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and pendants, uncertain; cf. Exod. 35.22. that expiation may be made for our persons before GOD.”

messages.text: These items are called: “The Lord’s offering,” but they are not called: “An offering to the Lord,” which is used only with regard to offerings sacrificed upon the altar.

notes.he: דההוא הוי משמע קרבן סתמא אבל השתא לא משמע קרבן סתמא:
notes.en: They are not called “an offering to the Lord”: for that would imply an offering without qualification; but as it is [“the Lord’s offering”], it does not imply an offering without qualification.

notes.dh: ולר' לא איקרו קרבן והכתיב כו'
notes.he: להאי לישנא קאמר השתא מאי ר' ומאי ר' שמעון דתנו רבנן וכו'. וללישנא אחרינא דקאמר לרבנן לא איקרי קרבן קסבר ההוא סתמא דמתני' דקתני קדשי בדק הבית אין עושין תמורה היינו רבנן מדלא איצטריך להו קרא למעוטינהו משום דסברי דלא איקרו קרבן ור' שמעון דקאמר והלא מעשר בכלל היה דמצריך למעוטינהו ממעשר אלמא משום דקסבר דאיקרו קרבן. וקאמר ולרבנן לא איקרו קרבן והכתיב כו'. דהכל במשמע שעושין תמורה ולהאי לישנא לא קא בעי מאי ר' ומאי ר' שמעון אלא מתחיל הברייתא דקתני תנו רבנן לא יבקר כו':
notes.en: And according to Rabbi they are not called an offering? But isn’t it written, etc.: according to this version, it now says: What is [the source of] Rabbi, and what is [the source of] Rabbi Shimon? As the Sages taught, etc. And according to the other version, which says: According to the Rabbis it is not called an offering, it holds that the anonymous mishna, which teaches: Items consecrated for Temple maintenance do not effect substitution, is the Rabbis, since they did not need a verse to exclude them, because they hold that they are not called an offering; and Rabbi Shimon, who says: But wasn’t the tithe included, needs to exclude them from the tithe, evidently because he holds that they are called an offering. And it says: And according to the Rabbis are they not called an offering? But isn’t it written, etc. For everything is implied [by “he shall not alter it”], that they effect substitution. And according to this version it does not ask: What is [the source of] Rabbi and what is [the source of] Rabbi Shimon, but begins the baraita that teaches: The Sages taught: “He shall not inquire,” etc.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that consecrated animals belonging to the community or to partners are not included in the halakha of substitution. The Sages taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: the community and partners do not render a non-sacred animal a substitute

notes.he:
ה"ג ת"ר לא יבקר כו'. ל"א גרסינן הא רבי הא ר"ש לר"ש איקרו קרבן לרבי לא איקרו קרבן - ולהאי לישנא פרשינן דבמתניתין ליכא פלוגתא אלא כולה ר"ש ודקתני קדשי בד"ה אינן עושין תמורה לאו מקרבן נפקא אלא ר"ש קאמר לה והדר מפרש טעמא הלכך ליכא למימר הא ר"ש הא רבנן:
הכי גרסינן להאי לישנא מאי רבי ומאי ר"ש דתניא לא יבקר בין טוב לרע וגו':
notes.en: This is the reading: The Sages taught: “He shall not inquire,” etc. Another version reads [in Rabbi Ḥanina’s answer]: This is Rabbi and that is Rabbi Shimon; according to Rabbi Shimon they are called an offering, according to Rabbi they are not called an offering. And according to this version we explain that in the mishna there is no dispute, but it is all Rabbi Shimon: that which it teaches, “Items consecrated for Temple maintenance do not effect substitution,” is not derived from “offering,” but Rabbi Shimon states it and then explains the reason. Therefore one cannot say: This is Rabbi Shimon and that is the Rabbis. For this version, this is the reading: What is [the source of] Rabbi, and what is [the source of] Rabbi Shimon? As it is taught: “He shall not inquire whether it is good or bad,” etc.

messages.text: The verse states with regard to the animal tithe: “He shall not inquire whether it is good or bad, neither shall he substitute it; and if he substitute it at all, then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be sacred; it shall not be redeemed” (Leviticus 27:33). Why is the issue of substitution stated here in connection to the animal tithe?

verse.he: לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין־טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ וְאִם־הָמֵר יְמִירֶנּוּ וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל׃
verse.en: One must not look out for good as against bad, or make substitution for it. If one does make substitution for it, then it and its substitute shall both be holy: it cannot be redeemed.

notes.he: האי קרא גבי מעשר והלא כבר נאמר לא יחליפנו וגו' דמשמע כל הקדשים עבדי תמורה ומעשר בכלל:
notes.en: Why is it stated: this verse with regard to the tithe? And wasn’t it already stated: “He shall not alter it,” etc., which implies that all consecrated animals effect substitution, and the tithe is included?

messages.text: Isn’t it already stated earlier: “He shall not alter it, nor substitute it, good for bad, or bad for good, and if he substitutes an animal for an animal, then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be sacred” (Leviticus 27:10)?

verse.he: לֹא יַחֲלִיפֶנּוּ וְלֹא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ טוֹב בְּרָע אוֹ־רַע בְּטוֹב וְאִם־הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: One may not exchange or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good; if one does substitute one animal for another, the thing vowed and its substitute shall both be holy.

messages.text: Since it is stated: “He shall not alter it, nor substitute it,” the verse apparently indicates that all types of offering are included, whether an individual offering or a communal offering, and whether it is an offering sacrificed on the altar or an offering consecrated for Temple maintenance. Therefore, the verse states with regard to the animal tithe: “He shall not inquire.”

notes.he: והאי ברייתא כולה רבי שמעון היא דאית ליה קדשי ב"ה איקרו קרבן ורבי שמעון קא מפרש טעמא ואזיל ואפילו ללישנא קמא הא ודאי כולה ר"ש היא דקתני תלמוד לומר לא יבקר וגו' כלומר להכי הדר כתיב תמורה גבי מעשר להקיש אליו שאר כל הקדשים כדקאמר רבי שמעון:
notes.en: And offerings of Temple maintenance: and this entire baraita is Rabbi Shimon, who holds that items consecrated for Temple maintenance are called an offering, and Rabbi Shimon goes on to explain the reason. And even according to the first version, this is certainly all Rabbi Shimon, as it teaches: “The verse states: He shall not inquire,” etc.; that is to say, it is for this that substitution was written again with regard to the tithe: to juxtapose all other consecrated animals to it, as Rabbi Shimon says.

messages.text: The animal tithe was included in the category of all offerings, and why was it singled out? It is to tell you: Just as the animal tithe is an individual offering, and an offering sacrificed on the altar, and it is an item that comes only as an obligation, not as a gift offering, and it is an item that is not brought in partnership, but only by an individual, so too, all offerings that render their substitutes sacred must be an individual offering, and an offering sacrificed on the altar, and it must be an item that comes only as an obligation,

notes.he: מפרשא לקמן למעוטי מאי:
notes.en: And an item of obligation: it is explained below what this excludes.

notes.he: כדפרישית לעיל יהיה לך ולא של שותפות:
notes.en: And an item that is not in partnership: as I explained above: “Shall be yours,” and not of partnership.

messages.text: and it must be an item that is not brought in partnership.

notes.dh: אמר ר' שמעון והלא מעשר כו'
notes.he: דהאי (לא ימירנו) [לא יבקר] אמעשר קאי. [ודבר שאינו בשותפות. כדאמר בפרק בתרא דבכורות יהיה לך ולא של שותפות אמר ר' להכי יצא מעשר]:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon said: But wasn’t the tithe, etc.: for this [“he shall not inquire”] refers to the tithe. [And an item that is not in partnership: as is said in the last chapter of Bekhorot: “Shall be yours,” and not of partnership. Rabbi said: For this the tithe was singled out.]

messages.text: Why was the animal tithe singled out of all offerings as subject to substitution now, after the halakha of substitution was stated in general? It serves to discuss a special halakha with regard to the animal tithe, that of substitution of its name. If, when the animals emerge from the pen to be tithed, the one counting them errs and calls the tenth animal the ninth and the eleventh the tenth, they are both sanctified. The animal that actually emerges tenth is the animal tithe, while the eleventh animal is consecrated as a peace offering.

notes.dh: רבי אומר למה יצא מעשר מעתה
notes.he: דסבירא ליה לרבי דמשום כל הני לא איצטריך דקרבן יחיד מלא ימיר נפקא דמשמע לשון יחיד וקרבן מזבח מקרבן נפקא אלמא אית ליה לרבי דקדשי בדק הבית לא איקרו קרבן ודבר שבחובה דקא ממעט ר"ש מיניה עולה הבא מן המותרות סבירא ליה לרבי מותרות לנדבת צבור אזלי ומרישא דמתני' נפקא לן דאין תמורה בצבור ושותפות נמי מלא ימיר לשון יחיד:
notes.en: Rabbi says: Why was the tithe singled out now: for Rabbi holds that it was not needed for all these. For an individual offering is derived from “he shall not substitute,” which is singular language; and an altar offering is derived from “offering”; evidently Rabbi holds that items consecrated for Temple maintenance are not called an offering. And as for an item of obligation, from which Rabbi Shimon excludes a burnt offering that comes from surplus, Rabbi holds that surplus goes to communal gift offerings, and from the first clause of the mishna we derive that there is no substitution for the community. And partnership too [is excluded] from “he shall not substitute,” singular language.

notes.he: דסבירא ליה לרבי דלקרבן יחיד ולמעוטי צבור ושותפין לא איצטריך שהרי כל הפרשה דתמורה בלשון יחיד נאמרה ולמעוטי נמי קדשי בדק הבית לא איצטריך דלא איקרו קרבן ולמעוטי נמי עולת מותרות לא איצטריך דקסבר עולת מותרות לנדבת צבור אזלי ופשיטא דלא עבדי תמורה כך פרש"י עוד י"ל דסבירא ליה דעולת מותרות לנדבת יחיד אזלי וסבר כרבי אליעזר דעושה תמורה:
notes.en: Rabbi says: Why was the tithe singled out: for Rabbi holds that it was not needed for an individual offering, to exclude the community and partners, since the whole passage of substitution is stated in singular language; and it was also not needed to exclude items consecrated for Temple maintenance, since they are not called an offering; and it was also not needed to exclude a burnt offering of surplus, since he holds that a burnt offering of surplus goes to communal gift offerings, and it is obvious that they do not effect substitution. So Rashi explained. One can further say that he holds that a burnt offering of surplus goes to an individual gift offering, and he holds like Rabbi Eliezer, that it effects substitution.

notes.he: היינו אם קרא לעשירי תשיעי ולתשיעי עשירי ולאחד עשר עשירי דקיימא לן (בכורות דף ס.) דשלשתן מקודשין:
notes.en: Substitution of its name: that is, if he called the tenth ninth, and the ninth tenth, and the eleventh tenth, for we maintain (Bekhorot 60a) that all three are consecrated.

messages.text: And since this halakha of a substitution of its name applies only to the animal tithe, it is necessary to teach that the general halakha of the substitution of its body, i.e., regular substitution, applies to it as well.

notes.dh: לפי שיצא מעשר לידון בתמורת שמו
notes.he: דכתיב לעיל מיניה ולכל מעשר ומרבינן מוכל לרבות שאם קרא לעשירי תשיעי ולאחד עשר עשירי שניהן קדושין והיינו תמורת שמו הלכך איצטריך למכתב נמי אם המר ימירנו לידון בתמורת גופו אם העמיד בהמת חולין אצל מעשר ואמר זו כזו נתפסת בתמורה דאי לא כתביה ה"א לא עביד תמורה כדאמרינן לקמן דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא לידון בדבר חדש דהיינו חידוש תמורת שמו שאינה בכל הקדשים והוי אמינא אין לך בו אלא חידושו תמורת שמו אבל תמורת גופו לא להכי אהדריה קרא ויצא לידון בתמורת שמו וגופו:
notes.en: Since the tithe was singled out to be discussed with regard to substitution of its name: as it is written earlier: “And all the tithe,” and we include from “all” that if he called the tenth ninth and the eleventh tenth, both are consecrated; and that is substitution of its name. Therefore it was necessary to write also: “And if he substitutes it at all,” to discuss substitution of its body: if he set a non-sacred animal beside the tithe and said: This is like this, it is seized as a substitute. For had [the verse] not written it, I would say it does not effect substitution, as we say below: an item that was included in a category and was singled out to be discussed with a new matter, which is the novelty of substitution of its name, which does not exist in all consecrated animals; and I would say: you have in it only its novelty, substitution of its name, but not substitution of its body. For this reason the verse repeated it, and it was singled out to be discussed with substitution of its name and of its body.

notes.he: דס"ד דאין עושין כלל תמורה משום דיצא לדון בדבר החדש כדמפרש הש"ס אי נמי לדון בתמורת גופו לומר דחלה על דבר שאינו ראוי ושניהן פירש רש"י:
notes.en: To discuss substitution of its body: for it would enter your mind that they do not effect substitution at all, since it was singled out to be discussed with a new matter, as the Talmud explains. Alternatively, “to discuss substitution of its body” means to say that it takes effect upon an item that is not fit. And Rashi explained both.

notes.he: דתמורת שמו [דמעשר] קרבה ותמורת גופו לא קרבה והיינו ולחלק [בין] תמורת שמו [לתמורת גופו] (קרבה) תמורת שמו היינו כדמפרש לקמן מנין שאם קרא תשיעי עשירי ולעשירי תשיעי ולאחד עשר עשירי תשיעי נאכל במומו ועשירי מעשר ואחד עשר קרב שלמים ועושה תמורה ומנלן דקדשי מדכתיב כל מעשר מרבויא דכל:
notes.en: To be discussed with substitution of its name and substitution of its body: for substitution of its name [of the tithe] is sacrificed and substitution of its body is not sacrificed; and this is [to distinguish between] substitution of its name [and substitution of its body]. Substitution of its name is as explained below: From where [is it derived] that if he called the ninth tenth, and the tenth ninth, and the eleventh tenth, the ninth is eaten in its blemished state, the tenth is tithe, and the eleventh is sacrificed as a peace offering and effects substitution? And from where do we derive that they are consecrated? Since it is written: “All the tithe,” from the inclusion of “all.”

messages.text: Furthermore, the verse tells you other halakhot unique to the animal tithe: An animal that is the substitute of the name of an animal tithe is sacrificed upon the altar as a peace offering, whereas the substitute of its body is not sacrificed at all. But for all other offerings, substitutes hold the same status as the animal for which they were substituted.

notes.he: כדאמרינן בשילהי בכורות (דף סא.) הבקר לרבות אחד עשר לשלמים:
notes.en: Substitution of its name is sacrificed: as we say at the end of Bekhorot (61a): “The herd” comes to include the eleventh as a peace offering.

notes.he: כדאמרינן בפירקין לעיל (תמורה דף ה:) גמר העברה העברה מבכור ובבכור כתיב הן הן קריבין ואין תמורתן קריבין:
notes.en: Substitution of its body is not sacrificed: as we say earlier in our chapter (Temurah 5b): [the tithe] derives “passing,” “passing” from the firstborn, and with regard to the firstborn it is written: “They” [are sacred]: they are sacrificed, and their substitutes are not sacrificed.

messages.text: Another difference is that the substitute of the name of an animal tithe is redeemed when it develops a blemish, like a peace offering, and the proceeds of the sale belong to the Temple treasury, whereas the substitute of its body is not redeemed, as it is stated with regard to the animal tithe: “Then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be sacred; it shall not be redeemed” (Leviticus 27:33).

verse.he: לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין־טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ וְאִם־הָמֵר יְמִירֶנּוּ וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל׃
verse.en: One must not look out for good as against bad, or make substitution for it. If one does make substitution for it, then it and its substitute shall both be holy: it cannot be redeemed.

notes.he: דשלמים היא ושלמים נגאלין כשנופל בהן מום:
notes.en: Substitution of its name is redeemed: for it is a peace offering, and peace offerings are redeemed when a blemish befalls them.

notes.he: דכתיב הוא ותמורתו יהיה קדש לא יגאל:
notes.en: Substitution of its body is not redeemed: as it is written: “Then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be sacred; it shall not be redeemed.”

notes.he: היינו תמורתו ממש [אינה קריבה דגמר מעשר עברה עברה מבכור וכתיב בבכור קדש הם הם ולא תמורתן. ותמורת שמו נגאלת מ"ט משום דשלמים נגאלין כשאר קדשים ותמורת שמו שלמים הוי ויש להן דין דשלמי'. תמורת גופו אין נגאלין דכתיב במעשר לא יגאל ותמורתן נמי] [כיוצא בו] תמורת גופו חלה על דבר שאינו ראוי לקרבן כגון בעל מום דכתיב לא ימיר אותו טוב ברע היינו בעל מום וכי היכי דחיילא תמורת מעשר אבעל מום הכי נמי חיילא אאתנן ומוקצה [ונעבד] דקי"ל דכל שאין המום פוסל בו אין דבר ערוה וע"ז פוסל בו:
notes.en: And substitution of its body: that is, its actual substitute [is not sacrificed, since the tithe derives “passing,” “passing” from the firstborn, and with regard to the firstborn it is written: “They are sacred”: they, and not their substitutes. And substitution of its name is redeemed. What is the reason? Because peace offerings are redeemed like other consecrated animals, and the substitution of its name is a peace offering and has the law of peace offerings. Substitution of its body is not redeemed, as it is written of the tithe: “It shall not be redeemed,” and their substitute likewise.] [Similarly,] substitution of its body takes effect upon an item that is not fit for an offering, such as a blemished animal, as it is written: “Nor substitute it, good for bad,” which is a blemished animal. And just as the substitution of the tithe takes effect upon a blemished animal, so too it takes effect upon a harlot’s payment, an animal set aside [for idolatry, and one that was worshipped], for we maintain that wherever a blemish does not disqualify, a matter of sexual transgression or idolatry does not disqualify.

messages.text: Finally, the sanctity of the substitution of the body of an animal tithe takes effect upon both an item that is fit for sacrifice upon the altar and upon an item that is unfit for sacrifice, e.g., a blemished animal, as the sanctity of the animal tithe can apply even to a blemished animal, but the substitution of its name takes effect only upon an item that is fit for sacrifice. If the animal that was mistakenly called the tenth is blemished, it is not consecrated.

notes.dh: תמורת גופו חלה אע"פ שאינו ראוי
notes.he: כגון בעל מום מאי טעמא כמעשר דחל על בעל מום ונפקא מינה לאכלו בקדושת מעשר שלא ישחט באיטליז ולא ישקל בליטרא:
notes.en: Substitution of its body takes effect even though it is not fit: such as a blemished animal. What is the reason? Like the tithe, which takes effect upon a blemished animal. And the practical difference is that it is eaten with the sanctity of the tithe: it is not slaughtered in the market and not weighed by the litra.

notes.dh: תמורת שמו אינה חלה אלא על דבר הראוי
notes.he: ליקדש קדושה גמורה כשאר קדשים שאינן חלים כשקדם מומן להקדשן:
notes.en: Substitution of its name takes effect only upon an item that is fit: to become consecrated with full sanctity, like other consecrated animals, upon which [sanctity] does not take effect when their blemish preceded their consecration.

notes.dh: ותמורת שמו אין חלה אלא על דבר הראוי
notes.he: ליקרב (למזבח) שלמים:
notes.en: And substitution of its name takes effect only upon an item that is fit: to be sacrificed as a peace offering.

messages.caption: Rabbi’s baraita: how the animal tithe’s substitution of its name differs from substitution of its body.

messages.text: Simply because the Merciful One includes a unique halakha with regard to the animal tithe, that it has the substitution of its name, would one assume that it is diminished, and the halakha of regular substitution does not apply to it?
messages.lead: The Sages say in response to the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi:

notes.dh: וקפריך משום דרבי ביה רחמנא דעביד תמורת שמו איגרועי מיגרעא
notes.he: דלא חיילא על בעל מום הא כ"ש דבעי למיזל ביה טפי לחומרא הואיל וחמור כל כך דאיתיה בתמורת שמו:
notes.en: And he asks: Because the Merciful One included with regard to it that it effects substitution of its name, is it diminished, so that it does not take effect upon a blemished animal? All the more so it should be treated more stringently, since it is so stringent that it has substitution of its name.

notes.he: מאי האי משום דרבי רחמנ' במעשר דאית ביה תמורת שמו איגרועי איגרע האי תמורת שמו מתמורת גופו דאילו תמורת גופו חלה על בעל מום קבוע ותמורת שמו לא חיילא על מום קבוע:
notes.en: They say: what is this? Because the Merciful One included in the tithe that it has substitution of its name, is this substitution of its name diminished compared with substitution of its body? For substitution of its body takes effect upon an animal with a permanent blemish, and substitution of its name does not take effect upon a permanent blemish.

messages.text: Yes, one can make such a claim, as we say: That which the verse included with regard to a particular halakha, it included, and that which it did not include, it did not include. Since the passage initially addresses substitution of name solely with regard to the animal tithe, one could assume that this is the only substitution that applies to it.

notes.he: וקרא לא רבי אלא מידי דחזי לשלמים כדקתני הבקר לרבות י"א לשלמים:
notes.en: What it included, it included: and the verse included only something that is fit for a peace offering, as it teaches: “The herd,” to include the eleventh as a peace offering.

notes.he: ודאי [דאמרינן] מאי דרבי בתמורת שמו רבי כגון דקרבה ונגאלת [כשלמים ומאי דלא רבי למיחל על דבר שאינו ראוי לא רבי:
notes.en: Yes: certainly [we say]: what it included in substitution of its name, it included, such as that it is sacrificed and redeemed [like peace offerings; and what it did not include, to take effect upon an item that is not fit, it did not include.]

messages.text: And from where would this be derived, that in this case we should assume only that which is specifically mentioned?

notes.he: דאמרינן הכי:
notes.en: From where would this come: that we say so?

notes.he: דאמרינן מאי דרבי רבי ומאי דלא רבי לא רבי אימא רבי לכל מילי:
notes.en: And from where would this come: that we say: what it included it included and what it did not include it did not include? Say that it included it for all matters.

messages.text: This is derived since this is a case of a matter, i.e., the animal tithe, where the Torah comes to discuss a novel matter, i.e., substitution of name, and as a rule, in such cases the object of discussion has only its novelty, and one cannot infer the applicability of additional principles. It was therefore necessary for a verse to teach that substitution of body, which applies to all other offerings, applies to the animal tithe as well.

notes.he: תמורת שמו:
notes.en: A new matter: substitution of its name.

notes.dh: לישנא אחרינא נתפרש תמורת שמו שאינה חלה אלא על דבר הראוי
notes.he: וסברא היא משום דאחמרא כשאר שלמים איגרועי מיגרע תמורת גופו איצטריך קרא לרבויי:
notes.en: Another version: [the baraita] explained that substitution of its name takes effect only upon an item that is fit, and this is logical, since it was made as stringent as other peace offerings. [The question] “is it diminished?” [concerns] substitution of its body, which a verse was needed to include.

notes.dh: ומשני אין דאי לא כתב ביה אמרינן למאי דרבי רבי כו' והא מהיכא תיתי
notes.he: דלימא הכי דהא אינה מן המדות שהתורה נדרשת בהן ואכתי למאי כתביה לידון בדבר חדש בתמורת שמו אין לך בו אלא חידושו להכי איצטריך לרבויי. והכי עיקר דללישנא דלעיל איכא תרי פירכי חדא דמאי קאמר למאי דרבי רבי לאו מילתא לאוקומה הכי דהא תמורת שמו דקדשה איתרבי מוכל מעשר בקר וצאן ולא משמע אלא סתמא בין תם בין בעל מום ומאי דרבי מהבקר לא רבי אלא להקרבה דלא תימא דלדייניה בתמורת גופו ועוד דקא פריך ליה מהיכא תיתי ואין זה לשון הש"ס הואיל ואוקים דודאי מיגרע גרעא דלמאי דלא רבי לא רבי הוה ליה למימר מנא לך הא דאמרינן הכי אבל להאי לישנא מישתמע שפיר מהיכא תיתי כלומר מהיכא אתיא לי דלימא הכי דאצרכה קרא לרבוייה:
notes.en: And he answers: Yes, for had it not been written with regard to it, we would say: What it included, it included, etc. And “from where would this come,” that we should say so, since this is not one of the principles by which the Torah is expounded? And still, why was it written? Since it comes to be discussed with a new matter, substitution of its name, you have in it only its novelty; therefore it was necessary to include it. And this is the main [explanation]. For according to the version above there are two difficulties. One: what does it mean by “what it included, it included”? There is no point in establishing it so, for substitution of its name, that it is consecrated, is included from “and all the tithe of the herd and the flock,” and that implies [an animal] without qualification, whether unblemished or blemished; and what it included from “the herd” it included only for sacrifice, so that you should not say we should judge it like substitution of its body. And further, it asks: “From where would this come?” and this is not the Talmud’s language, since it established that it is certainly diminished, for what it did not include, it did not include; it should have said: From where do you have this, that we say so? But according to this version, “from where would this come” is well understood; that is to say: from where does it come to me that we should say so, so that a verse was needed to include it?

notes.he: שיצא לידון בדבר החדש דתמורת שמו קרבה ונגאלת] מה שאין כן בתמורת גופו הילכך אין לך בו אלא חדושו בלבד:
notes.en: Rav Huna said: because it was singled out to be discussed with a new matter, that substitution of its name is sacrificed and redeemed,] which is not so for substitution of its body; therefore you have in it only its novelty alone.

messages.text: § @Rava According to the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who said earlier that the halakha of substitution applies only to offerings that come as an obligation, should one conclude that it is only an obligatory burnt offering that renders an animal exchanged for it a substitute, but a voluntary burnt offering does not?

A voluntary burnt offering also falls under the category of obligatory offerings. Since he accepted upon himself to bring a voluntary burnt offering, it is considered an obligation for him, and therefore it renders an animal exchanged for it a substitute.
messages.quote: but a voluntary burnt offering does not?

notes.he: שיקריבנה ואע"ג דאמר הרי זו:
notes.en: Since he accepted it upon himself: to sacrifice it, even though he said: This is [a burnt offering].

messages.text: And this qualification mentioned by Rabbi Shimon is necessary only to exclude a burnt offering that came from surplus funds. For example, if one set aside a certain sum of money for a sin offering or a guilt offering, and after purchasing his animal some of the money remained, he must purchase a burnt offering with that money. The halakha of substitution does not apply to such an animal.

notes.he: כגון אשם שניתק לרעייה דדמיו קריבין עולה וכגון הפריש מעות לחטאתו ואשמו וניתותרו מביא באותן דמים עולה דזהו מדרש יהוידע הכהן כל הבא ממותר חטאת וממותר אשם ילקח בהן עולות הבשר לשם והעורות לכהנים בפרק ולד חטאת (לקמן תמורה דף כג:):
notes.en: Surplus: such as a guilt offering that was consigned to grazing, whose money is brought as a burnt offering; and such as one who set aside money for his sin offering and his guilt offering and some was left over: he brings a burnt offering with that money. For this is the exposition of Jehoiada the priest: Whatever comes from the surplus of a sin offering and from the surplus of a guilt offering, burnt offerings are to be bought with it, the meat to God and the hides to the priests, in the chapter Velad Ḥatat (below, Temurah 23b).

notes.he: ההיא דקאמר ודבר שבא חובה אלא למעוטי]:
notes.en: [It is necessary only: that which he said, “an item that comes as an obligation,” is only to exclude:]

messages.text: The Sages disputed the use of surplus money. Some say that it must go toward the purchase of communal burnt offerings, whereas Rabbi Eliezer maintains that the owner himself must purchase a voluntary burnt offering. What does Rabbi Shimon hold in this regard?
messages.quote: a burnt offering that came from surplus funds

messages.text: If he holds in accordance with the one who said that these surplus funds go toward communal gift offerings, then it is obvious that this offering does not render a substitute, as it is explicitly taught that there is no substitution with regard to a communal offering. Rabbi Shimon’s statement would then be redundant.

notes.he: לשופרות:
notes.en: Go to communal gift offerings: to the horn-shaped collection chests.

notes.he: כגון (שהקדיש) [שהפריש] מעות לחובתו וניתותרו מהן דההיא לא עבדא תמורה. דהא אמרי רבנן מותרות לנדבת ציבור אזלן וציבור לא עבדי תמורה:
notes.en: A burnt offering that comes from surplus: such as one who set aside money for his obligation and some of it was left over; that one does not effect substitution. For the Rabbis said that surplus goes to communal gift offerings, and the community does not effect substitution.

messages.text: Rather, say that Rabbi Shimon holds in accordance with the one who said that these surplus funds go toward the voluntary burnt offering of an individual. But this too is problematic, as whom did you hear who holds this reasoning? It is Rabbi Eliezer, but we heard that Rabbi Eliezer explicitly stated that such an animal renders an animal exchanged for it a substitute. As it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: הבעלים עצמן מביאין בדמים עולה ואינה עולה להן לחובתן אלא לשם דורון הוא:
notes.en: To an individual gift offering: the owners themselves bring a burnt offering with the money, and it does not count for their obligation; rather, it is as a gift.

notes.he: דאית ליה מותרות לנדבת יחיד אזלי בפרק ואלו קדשים (לקמן תמורה דף כ:) תמורת אשם ולד תמורה ולדן ולד ולדן עד סוף העולם ירעו עד שיסתאבו וימכרו ויפלו דמיהן לנדבה לשופרות רבי אליעזר אומר יביא בדמיו עולה:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer: who holds that surplus goes to an individual gift offering, in the chapter Ve’elu Kodashim (below, Temurah 20b): The substitute of a guilt offering, the offspring of a substitute, their offspring and the offspring of their offspring until the end of the world, shall graze until they become blemished, and they are sold and their money goes to gift offerings, to the horn-shaped chests. Rabbi Eliezer says: He brings a burnt offering with its money.

messages.text: A burnt offering that came from surplus funds renders a non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it consecrated as a substitute. This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

Rabbi Shimon holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer with regard to one matter, that surplus funds go toward an individual voluntary burnt offering, and disagrees with him with regard to another matter, as Rabbi Eliezer maintains that a burnt offering that came from surplus funds renders a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute, and he, Rabbi Shimon, maintains that it does not render it a substitute.

notes.he: דמותרות לנדבת יחיד אזלי דלהכי אצטריך למעוטיה מתמורה:
notes.en: He agrees with him in one: that surplus goes to an individual gift offering; that is why it was necessary to exclude it from substitution.

messages.caption: Rabbi Shimon’s lesson from the animal tithe: four features an offering needs for its substitute to be sacred, and what each one excludes.

messages.text: If so, consider that dilemma raised by Rabbi Avin:

notes.he: דלרבי שמעון עולת הבהמה מותרות לא עבדה תמורה ואפילו לא אמיר בה מעיקרא לא מצי אמיר בה השתא דעולה הבאה מן המותרות היא:
notes.en: If so: that according to Rabbi Shimon a burnt offering of surplus does not effect substitution, then even if he had not substituted for it at first, he could not substitute for it now, for it is a burnt offering that comes from surplus.

messages.text: If one separated an animal as a guilt offering by which to achieve atonement, and he effected substitution for it, and then that original guilt offering developed a blemish and he redeemed it with another animal, which he subsequently lost, and the owner achieved atonement by bringing yet another animal as a guilt offering; and then this lost animal was found and consigned to be sacrificed as a burnt offering, what is the halakha as to whether he can again effect substitution for it?

notes.he: אי נמי נתכפר באשם אחר כו' כדפרישית לעיל בפירקין:
notes.en: And he desacralized it onto another: alternatively, he achieved atonement with another guilt offering, etc., as I explained above in our chapter. [Rashi’s text of the dilemma includes “and he desacralized it onto another,” which the Aramaic printed here lacks; the Davidson English supplies it.]

notes.he: דהיכא אמר רבי יוחנן אליבא דרבי שמעון אין ממירין וחוזרין וממירין היכא דקאים בקדושתיה אבל כגון קדושה אחרת לימא דמימר או דילמא ל"ש:
notes.en: May he again substitute for it: for where Rabbi Yoḥanan said, according to Rabbi Shimon, that one does not substitute and again substitute, that is where it remains in its sanctity; but, for example, with another sanctity, shall we say that he can substitute, or perhaps there is no difference?

notes.he: זה ראשון לעולה משום דנמצא לאחר כפרה [והיינו] עולה הבאה מן המותרות [הא קא מיבעיא ליה:
notes.en: And this was consigned: this first one, to a burnt offering, because it was found after atonement; [and that is] a burnt offering that comes from surplus. [That is what he asks.]

messages.text: In this case, the animal in question is a burnt offering that came from surplus funds.

In accordance with whose opinion was this dilemma raised? If we say it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, you said that Rabbi Shimon maintains that a burnt offering that came from surplus funds does not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute. There would therefore be no dilemma at all. This is problematic, because the dilemma assumes that one cannot effect substitution twice for the same animal, which is the opinion of Rabbi Shimon.
messages.quote: he can again effect substitution for it

notes.dh: אי אליבא דרבי שמעון ממעשר ילפינן
notes.he: כלומר הא דגמר ר' שמעון ממעשר דבר שבחובה לאפוקי עולת מותר דלא עבדה תמורה:
notes.en: If according to Rabbi Shimon, we derive from the tithe: that is to say, that which Rabbi Shimon derived from the tithe, an item of obligation, to exclude a burnt offering of surplus, which does not effect substitution.

notes.he: ל"א אי אליבא דר' שמעון דאמר ממעשר ילפינן אפי' חדא תמורה נמי לא עבדא דהא אמר מה מעשר שבא חובה עושה תמורה (ואפי') ועולה הבאה מן המותרות אינה באה חובה:
notes.en: Another version: If according to Rabbi Shimon, who said we derive from the tithe, it does not effect even one substitution, for he said: just as the tithe, which comes as an obligation, effects substitution; and a burnt offering that comes from surplus does not come as an obligation.

messages.text: This is the dilemma that Rabbi Avin was raising: If a tanna is found who holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who said that one cannot effect substitution once and again effect substitution for the same consecrated animal, and he also holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, who said that a burnt offering that came from surplus funds renders a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute, what is his opinion as to whether one can again effect substitution with the animal in question?

notes.he: דסבירא ליה כרבי אליעזר וכר' יוחנן דאמר לעיל אליבא דר"ש אין ממירין וחוזרין וממירין כו':
notes.en: If you find a tanna: who holds like Rabbi Eliezer and like Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said above, according to Rabbi Shimon, that one does not substitute and again substitute, etc.

notes.he: והכי קא מיבעיא ליה אי סבירא ליה לר' אלעזר כר' שמעון דאמר אין מימר וחוזר ומימר הני מילי בחד גופה בב' גופין וקדושה אחת מאי היינו בלא נתכפר:
notes.en: And this is what he asks: if Rabbi Elazar [the daf reads Rabbi Eliezer] holds like Rabbi Shimon, who says one does not substitute and again substitute, that applies only to one body; in two bodies and one sanctity, what? That is, where he did not achieve atonement [with another].

messages.text: As explained earlier (9b), Rabbi Avin’s dilemma was first posed with regard to two bodies, i.e., two different animals, and one type of sanctity, e.g., in a case where one separated an animal as a guilt offering, and he effected substitution for it, and the animal he separated as a guilt offering developed a blemish and he redeemed it with another animal, which assumed the same status of a guilt offering. What is the halakha as to whether one can substitute for this replacement? Do we say that since it is a different animal from the one for which he initially effected substitution, the second substitution is effective? Or perhaps, since it possesses the same sanctity as the original animal, one cannot effect substitution for it.

notes.he: דהיינו הפריש אשם להתכפר בו והמיר בו והומם וחיללו על אחר:
notes.en: In two bodies and one sanctity, what: that is, he set aside a guilt offering to achieve atonement with it, and substituted for it, and it became blemished and he desacralized it onto another.

messages.text: And then Rabbi Avin further asked: If you say that in the above case one cannot effect substitution for the animal, perhaps this is only because the two animals possess one sanctity. But in a case of two sanctities and one body, what is the halakha? For example, if one consecrated a guilt offering and effected substitution for it, and he subsequently lost it and atoned using another animal, and he then found it again, such that the original animal must now be consigned to be sacrificed as a burnt offering, does one say that since the animal now possesses a different sanctity he can effect further substitution for it?

notes.he: דהיינו נתכפר באשם אחר ונמצא ראשון האבוד וניתק לעולה:
notes.en: But two sanctities and one body: that is, he achieved atonement with another guilt offering, and the first, lost one was found and was consigned to a burnt offering.

notes.he: היינו בלא הומם מאי מי חוזר ומימר בגוף אחד וקדושה אחרת מאי תיבעי]:
notes.en: And two sanctities and one body: that is, where it did not become blemished. What? May he again substitute with one body and a different sanctity? What? Tiba’ei.]

messages.text: According to that tanna, the dilemma remains unresolved [tiba’ei].

notes.he: לשון ירושלמי כמו תיקו בלשון בבלי:
notes.en: Tiba’ei: the language of the Jerusalem [Talmud], like teiku in the language of the Babylonian [Talmud].

notes.he: הדרן עלך הכל ממירין
notes.en: We will return to you, HaKol Memirin.

messages.text: הדרן עלך הכל ממירין · Hadran alakh HaKol Memirin: we will return to you, chapter 1, “Everyone Substitutes.”
Chapter 2 · יש בקרבנות · Yesh BaKorbanot: halakhot that apply to offerings of an individual and not to communal offerings, and to communal offerings and not to those of an individual.
Continues on 14a with the chapter’s opening mishna: offerings of an individual render a non-sacred animal exchanged for them a substitute, and communal offerings do not.
